uncited: **Global Transformation:** The input 3D scalar volume $f(x, y, z)$ is transformed into a global representation in an alternative domain.
**Slice Extraction:** A 2D slice or projection is extracted from the global representation corresponding to the desired viewing direction.

In frequency-domain methods, this relies on the **Projection-Slice Theorem**, which states that the 2D Fourier transform of a projection is equal to a central slice of the 3D Fourier transform perpendicular to the viewing direction [S3, 824-fourier-projection-slice-volume-rendering.md].

Since the slicing plane rarely aligns with the discrete lattice of the transformed data, interpolation (e.g., trilinear, tri-cubic, or windowed sinc) is required to resample the data onto a 2D grid [S3, 952-frequency-domain-volume-rendering.md].
*   **Boundary Artifacts:** Transforms assume periodic boundary conditions.
Discontinuities at volume boundaries cause high-frequency artifacts (ghosting).

Mitigation includes zero-padding the volume by a factor of $k_2$ (typically $4/3$) and applying vignetting correction (premultiplying by the reciprocal of the interpolation filter response) [S4, S5, 824-fourier-projection-slice-volume-rendering.md].
